<description>
{
 "summary": "Optimizes peer address grouping and ASMap lookups in AddrMan by eliminating unnecessary heap allocations, redundant network classifications, and integer decoding overhead. When ASMap is disabled or empty, GetMappedAS returns early without re-classifying the address; with ASMap enabled, lookup keys are constructed on the stack and vector capacity for group tags is pre-reserved. The PR also adds microbenchmarks and unit tests covering ASN byte-order and IPv4-mapped address variants.",
 "problem": "AddrMan groups peer addresses frequently, but without ASMap configured it redundantly classifies each address twice. When ASMap is active, each lookup allocates a temporary key on the heap, repeatedly calculates mantissa shift distances during integer decoding, and triggers multiple reallocations when building the small group byte vector.",
 "evidence": [
  "Author microbenchmarks on a Raspberry Pi 5 show AddrManAdd running 19.2% faster overall (59.1 ms to 49.6 ms) across the patch set (PR description).",
  "Individual grouping benchmarks report IPv4 group calculation dropping from 518 ns to 307 ns without ASMap (approx. 40% reduction) and from 1,982 ns to 1,640 ns with ASMap (approx. 17% reduction) (PR description, commit 4131eaa53f)."

<category name="p2p" title="P2P">
## Covers

Everything between this node and other nodes: connection management and
peer selection, address management, the message protocol and its
transport (including the encrypted v2 transport), block and transaction
relay including compact blocks, headers sync, transaction request and
orphan handling, network-level DoS protections, and the Tor, I2P, and
CJDNS integrations. The P2P and Private Broadcast labels are a strong
prior.

Not p2p: what the node does with a block or transaction once received
(validation, mempool); RPCs that merely report peer state (rpc).

## What matters here

Resistance to attack first: eclipse and partition resistance, DoS
resistance in message handling and resource accounting, and privacy of
transaction origin. Then relay correctness and liveness: blocks and
transactions propagate reliably and quickly, and nothing gets stuck.
Then interoperability with the rest of the network and with new
protocol features (BIPs) that other software depends on. Then bandwidth
and resource use, which node operators feel. Then connectivity across
network types and platforms.

Protocol changes with a specification and other implementations
waiting rank higher than local optimizations. Refactors count when they
retire a known hazard in message handling.
